body:
GitHub issue #141.

## Problem

Landing any legitimate change to a trust root (`scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs`,
`docs/ci/rails-guard.yml`, the hash fixture, `.adlc/tickets*`, CODEOWNERS)
means the `rails-guard` CI check goes RED by design (the gate self-protects:
rails-guard-ci.mjs:428-434 denies on any diff to `immutableTrustRoots`), and a
human clicks admin-merge to override the red required check. The audit trail is
just 'someone used --admin', and it TRAINS operators to override a red security
gate — a bad reflex. Lived concretely in Wave 1 completing T62/T70 (had to
complete on protected main directly / admin path).

## Design — CODEOWNERS-gated authorized-change ceremony

Authorization is a non-author CODEOWNERS APPROVING REVIEW plus an explicit
`trust-root-change` label. The label is intent; the approval is authorization
(GitHub forbids self-approval, so an author cannot self-authorize).

- `rails-guard-ci.mjs`: when a trust-root diff is present, determine
  authorization from PR context (label + reviews), gathered via the read-only
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` (GitHub API). If AUTHORIZED -> do NOT deny: print the authorized
  approver and record a `trust-root-authorized` manifest entry (approver, the
  changed trust-root paths, the head SHA). If NOT authorized -> deny exactly as
  today. Locally / no GitHub context -> unchanged deny with the protected-base
  guidance (never auto-authorize without a verifiable approval).
- The security backstop is GitHub BRANCH PROTECTION requiring CODEOWNERS review
  for the trust-root paths (GitHub-enforced, a PR cannot tamper it). The script
  check makes the `rails-guard` signal GREEN + AUDITED for authorized changes; it
  is NOT the sole boundary (a PR that tampers the script to skip the deny still
  cannot merge without the CODEOWNERS approval branch protection requires).
- NO signing key is exposed to PR CI (T36 rejected manifest-signature approaches
  for exactly this reason). Read-only token + review state only.

## Required behavior

1. Extract a PURE function, e.g. `classifyTrustRootAuthorization({ label, reviews,
   author, owners })` -> `{ authorized: boolean, approver: string|null,
   reason: string }`. Authorized IFF: the `trust-root-change` label is present
   AND at least one APPROVED review is from an owner in `owners` (the CODEOWNERS
   of the trust-root paths) who is NOT the PR author. Dismissed/stale/
   commented/author reviews do not count.
2. Wire it into rails-guard-ci.mjs's trust-root check: authorized -> allow +
   record; else -> deny.
3. The CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml rails-guard) and the user template
   (docs/ci/rails-guard.yml) pass the PR number + `GITHUB_TOKEN` so the script
   can read labels/reviews; document the `trust-root-change` label + the branch-
   protection CODEOWNERS-review requirement it depends on.
4. Record a `trust-root-authorized` gate-manifest entry on an authorized change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A trust-root PR with the `trust-root-change` label AND a non-author CODEOWNER
   approval passes `rails-guard` (exit 0) and records a `trust-root-authorized`
   manifest entry naming the approver. Verify via the unit test of the pure
   classifier + a recorded-entry assertion.
2. Without the label, OR with only the author's own (self) approval, OR with a
   non-CODEOWNER approval, OR with a dismissed/stale approval -> still DENIED.
   Verify: table-driven unit tests over the classifier, each case RED-if-flipped.
3. The author cannot self-authorize: an approval whose reviewer == PR author is
   never sufficient. Verify by a dedicated case.
4. No GitHub context available (local run) -> behavior is unchanged (deny with
   the existing protected-base guidance); the ceremony never auto-authorizes
   without a verifiable non-author CODEOWNER approval.
5. This ticket's own trust-root changes are themselves landed via the ceremony
   (or the final admin-override that bootstraps it) — documented in the PR.
6. CODEOWNERS covers every path in `immutableTrustRoots`; the workflow-hash
   drift fixture is updated for the template change. Full suite + preflight green.

## Constraints

- Do NOT weaken the default deny: absence of a verifiable non-author CODEOWNER
  approval must fail closed exactly as today.
- Do NOT expose a signing key or any write-scoped secret to PR CI.
- Keep the authorization decision a PURE, unit-tested function; the GitHub API
  I/O (fetching label/reviews) is a thin, separately-testable adapter.
- This is a trust-root change (rails-guard-ci.mjs, docs/ci/rails-guard.yml,
  CODEOWNERS, ci.yml) -> P5 is cross-model gated; it bootstraps via one final
  admin-override.
title: Trust-root change ceremony: a CI-recognized authorized path instead of admin-override of a red rails-guard check
